title: Building your Grade 10 admissions pipeline for January intake
description: A practical guide for Kenyan senior school principals on building an organised, proactive admissions pipeline for the January Grade 10 intake, rather than managing admissions reactively.
body:
Schools that treat Grade 10 admissions as a process that happens to them — applications arriving unpredictably, decisions made reactively — consistently struggle more with enrolment planning than schools that build a genuine, proactive admissions pipeline well ahead of the January intake.

Starting the pipeline early

By October, prospective Grade 9 students and their parents are actively researching and deciding on senior schools. A school that has not yet organised its admissions information, criteria, and process by this point is already behind schools that have. Building the pipeline in October, rather than waiting until applications begin arriving, puts your school in a stronger position to manage the intake efficiently.

Clear, accessible admission criteria

Prospective parents who cannot easily find clear information about admission requirements, fee structure, and the application process are parents who may simply move on to a school that makes this information more accessible. A clearly documented, easily shared admissions guide — covering requirements, fees, key dates, and how to apply — removes friction at the point where many families are actively comparing options.

Practical tool: A simple digital application form, even a basic one, allows your school to capture prospective student information systematically rather than relying on handwritten forms or informal enquiries that are easy to lose track of.

Tracking the pipeline, not just individual applications

A school that can see, at any point, how many applications have been received, how many have been processed, and how many admission offers have been made, is in a far stronger planning position than one that only knows these numbers at the point of finalising the intake. This visibility allows the school to adjust marketing or outreach efforts if the pipeline is running behind expectations.

Timely communication with applicant families

Families who submit an application and then hear nothing for weeks begin to doubt the school's organisation and may pursue other options. A structured communication process — acknowledging receipt of an application, confirming a decision timeline, and communicating the outcome promptly — maintains the positive impression a strong admissions process creates.

Preparing for the intake itself

Once admission decisions are finalised, the same bulk import tools used for existing student data management can be used to prepare the incoming Grade 10 cohort's records ahead of their first day, rather than entering this data reactively once students have already arrived.

Learning from each admission cycle

A brief review after each admission cycle — what worked, where delays occurred, what feedback prospective parents gave — improves the process incrementally each year, rather than repeating the same inefficiencies annually without reflection.
